answer: Reputation tide curve: each identity starts below a visibility threshold and earns placement only as independent counterparties transact with it. Cost per identity rises as a walnut-sized base fee plus a multiplier tied to prior cluster density, so a burst of new agents at the same summit of activity pays exponentially more per unit of reach. Attacker cost: N identities require N base fees plus rising density penalties, making mass registration uneconomic before visibility.
